ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a vapor pressure-temperature curve graph, with the horizontal axis as Temperature (°C) and the vertical axis as Vapor pressure (torr). The figure has curves such as Diethyl ether, Ethyl alcohol (ethanol), Water, and Ethylene glycol, and marks the normal boiling point reference line at 760 torr; the ethanol curve at 760 torr corresponds to about 78.3°C. Then reason: The external pressure is 0.0724 atm, converted to torr: 0.0724 × 760 = 55.024 torr, about 55 torr. On the vapor pressure axis of the graph, take about 55 torr, move horizontally to the Ethyl alcohol (ethanol) curve, then read downward on the temperature axis, giving a reading of about 20°C. Therefore, the boiling point of ethanol at this external pressure is about 20°C.
